summary:
Normandie stands under the national framework of France. Rules on identity documents, anti-discrimination protection, criminal law and marriage apply uniformly across all regions and departments, and the sources reviewed record no division-specific transgender findings for this region apart from one custodial inspection visit.

For a transgender visitor, the documented risks concentrate in two settings: detention and the border. In ordinary movement, accommodation and services, France's own oversight bodies record persistent discrimination rather than legal prohibition.

Prison placement follows no dedicated statutory rule for trans detainees. Article D248 of the French Criminal Procedure Code requires men and women to be held in separate establishments, so trans women whose identity documents record a male sex — the vast majority of those held — are placed in men's facilities. A BuzzFeed News feature of 12 January 2018 reports a detainee recalling other inmates shouting "We don't want any women here!" alongside threats of violence, and quotes Adeline Hazan, controller-general of places of deprivation of liberty, that transgender detainees, overwhelmingly women, are the group that suffers most in prison; the feature illustrates this with an American trans woman, Kara B., held in conditions Hazan described as worrying.

The CGLPL, France's national custodial-inspection authority, issued an opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty, following its opinion of 30 June 2010. It records continuing serious violations of the fundamental rights of trans detainees in adult prisons, while noting none in mental-health establishments, closed educational centres or juvenile detention centres. The review covered roughly forty transgender detainees, with interviews including eight trans women and one trans man, and inspection visits at Fleury-Mérogis, Caen, Saint-Martin-de-Ré and Toulouse-Seysses prisons and the Toulouse central police station. The Caen establishment is the one inspected site within this region.

At entry points, trans women have faced questioning of their identity documents in public. Giovanna Rincon's first-person account in StreetPress of 7 March 2017 describes ten minutes of routine humiliation by French border police at an airport, questioned in front of other travellers.

The Défenseur des droits has issued a framework decision on trans rights confirming persistent fundamental-rights violations drawn from case files and association testimony. It cites the European Union Fundamental Rights Agency's 2023 survey, in which 64% of trans people in France report identity-related discrimination, and sets out official guidance for service providers.

For partner recognition, the baseline dates from the marriage-equality law in force by late May 2013; France's first same-sex wedding was reported on 29 May 2013, performed days after the law took effect.
tangentialFactors:
The 2021 CGLPL opinion is a follow-up to an opinion of 30 June 2010, and the authority has examined around forty referrals from trans detainees since 2010 together with ministry and association input. The national preventive mechanism explained that a new opinion was needed because the earlier one produced no marked improvement, because the gender-recognition law and its terminology had changed after the 2016 legal gender-recognition reform, and because coverage now extends to intersex and non-binary detainees. Its findings rest on a decade of letters from detained trans people and identify structural problems in the isolation of vulnerable detainees and in suicide prevention.

Accounts collected in the BuzzFeed News feature of 12 January 2018 describe heightened assault vulnerability and suicide risk under improvised placement arrangements, with treatment varying between establishments; the sources describe special units and isolation restricting contact with other inmates as the responses in use.

Placement remained current as an issue in 2025. Louna, a trans woman detained for opposing the A69 motorway works, has been held since mid-October 2024 in the Tarbes men's prison and kept in isolation since October. Her incarceration was raised before the Keeper of the Seals in oral question no. 219 in the French National Assembly, arguing that the case exposes a prison system unable to guarantee conditions for trans detainees.

The divergence between settings matters for expectations: serious violations were recorded in adult prisons and not in mental-health establishments, closed educational centres or juvenile detention centres, so risk in custody depends on which kind of facility a person is held in.
localsOnly:
The Défenseur des droits framework decision is addressed to residents as well as visitors: it sets out official guidance for service providers drawing on case files and association testimony, and can be used to press a complaint about discrimination in services in Normandie.

The 64% figure for identity-related discrimination reported by trans people in France comes from the EU Fundamental Rights Agency's 2023 survey and describes the lived situation of residents, who encounter discrimination in employment, housing and public services rather than a legal prohibition on being trans.

Residents placed in custody under Article D248 face the same document-based placement logic as any detainee, and the CGLPL inspection of Caen prison makes that establishment within this region one of the documented sites of review.

Marriage and partner recognition for same-sex couples rests on the law in force by late May 2013, which applies to residents marrying in France.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Normandie-specific enforcement data on border checks, document markers or service refusal was located in the sources reviewed; the region-specific material consists of the Caen prison inspection visit recorded in the CGLPL opinion of 25 May 2021.

Whether placement decisions at Caen or any other establishment within the region differ from the national pattern described under Article D248 is not sourced.

The sources reviewed do not state whether the CGLPL's findings on isolation and strip-search exposure have been implemented in this region, and no post-2021 regional inspection outcome was available.

Regional data on access to gender-affirming care, on changing identity documents for people resident in Normandie, and on outcomes of discrimination complaints lodged with the Défenseur des droits in this region are not sourced here.
